title: Graceful preempt broker with KV working-set shaping and soft-resume
creator: Daniel Cho
summary: Introduce a preemption broker that performs soft-yield, KV working-set shaping, and per-tenant GPU residency quotas to meet latency SLOs while maximizing throughput.
description:
Background: Continuous batching is our primary throughput lever for hosted inference, but high KV cache residency and large per-request working sets can cause tenants to exceed GPU memory and trigger hard evictions or long GC-like pauses. Existing preemptors are either aggressive (hard-preempt, high latency impact) or too passive (miss SLOs under memory pressure). This ticket proposes a graceful preemption broker that combines soft-resume semantics, KV working-set shaping (HWM/LWM watermarks), per-tenant cgroup-like GPU residency quotas, and an adaptive grace timer keyed to observed tail-latency distributions.

Goals: 1) Keep P95/P99 latency within tenant SLOs under mixed workloads. 2) Reduce hard-kv-evictions and full-model reloads by shaping working sets before eviction. 3) Maximize token throughput by enabling safe background batch draining and opportunistic merging of buffered requests. 4) Provide clear observability for preemption decisions and the resulting KV residency changes.

Proposal overview:
- Preemption broker runs per-device and exposes a policy API: {latency_budget_ms, kv_target_residency_mb, grace_window_ms, resume_strategy}. (Config is persisted in per-tenant profile.)
- Soft-yield: rather than immediate cancel, the broker signals prioritized requests to enter a soft-yield state where they stop accepting new tokens for up to grace_window_ms while their KV footprint is checkpointed to a fast LRU segment and in-flight micro-batches are flushed. If the request doesn't resume within grace_window_ms, it transitions to a resumable preempted state rather than hard-canceled; state includes compacted KV pointers and partial output.
- KV working-set shaping: implement HWM/LWM watermarks per-tenant. When above HWM, broker instructs the runtime to compact KV (drop low-utility entries attenuated by access recency and token-likelihood score) to reach kv_target_residency_mb. When under LWM, the tenant is eligible for aggressive batching.
- Residency quotas: light-weight soft cgroups enforce a max GPU residency per-tenant. Excess residency triggers a cooperative shrink process (compaction + soft-yield) with backoff.
- Adaptive policy: broker samples tail latency, KV eviction rate, and successful resume rate; it increases grace_window_ms when resume rate is high and reduces it when it sees many timeouts. It biases preemption away from tenants with high success-rate and towards non-critical background tenants.

Design doc and artifacts: design doc linked in design_links below contains sequence diagrams, state machine, and proto changes.

Rollout plan: feature gated behind runtime flag 'preempt_broker_v2' and tenant opt-in. Start in Canary on dedicated pools with low customer impact, evaluate telemetry for 2 weeks, then flip on for low-tier hosted and evaluate again before broader rollout.

Acceptance criteria: see acceptance_criteria field.

Risks & mitigations: see risks field.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Under a mixed workload benchmark (50% high-kv long-context, 50% short requests) running on a 4xA100 instance, P99 latency for tiered SLO tenants must not regress more than 10% vs baseline and P95 must be within SLO. 2) KV hard-eviction count reduced by >=40% over 24h compared to baseline while maintaining >=95% request resume success. 3) Metrics exposed: preempt_decisions_total, soft_yield_count, resume_success_rate, kv_compactions_total, per_tenant_residency_mb. 4) No increase in OOM crashes during canary period.
implementation_notes:
Key changes: add broker RPC and policy store; extend runtime to accept soft-yield and compact-kv commands; implement lightweight per-tenant residency accounting; add background compaction worker with token-bucket to limit work during peak token generation. Must add end-to-end tests that simulate resumable state restore and measure resume_time_ms distribution. Keep PRs small and reviewable.

Performance considerations: compaction must be O(n) with small constants; prefer probabilistic sampling for low-utility KV entries instead of full scan. Use a write-ahead compact log to allow quick rollback if resume fails.

Migration: older clients ignore soft-yield and will get hard-preempt behavior; document compatibility in migration guide.
risks: Incorrect compaction heuristics can drop useful KV tokens causing quality regressions
Long grace windows could increase memory pressure if resumptions are slow
Complexity in state serialization could cause slow resume times and double-accounting of KV residency
open_questions: What is the right heuristic for token-likelihood scoring in KV compaction? (frequency vs recency vs model-informed)
Should resume state be stored in device-local NVM or external object store for larger contexts?
What SLA tiers opt in by default? (we should avoid gating enterprise customers without discussion)
